guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Adult Basic Life Support 2021 (Choking)
title: Elderly choking episode at a care home fun day
setting: Care home fun day. An elderly resident (Joyce) shouts for help. Her daughter (Grace, 52F) is clutching her throat, unable to speak, gasp, or cough.
verdictExplanation: Severe complete airway obstruction (unable to speak, cough, or breathe). Choking is a critical life-threatening emergency. Sick: deliver immediate back blows and abdominal thrusts.

shared.danger: Hot coffee cup on the table
shared.response: Responding to voice with wild, panicked gestures
shared.circulation: Tachycardic, face is puffy and deeply flushed/cyanosed

history.history: Choked on a hard gingersnap biscuit while eating and talking with her mother
history.additional: Mother Joyce is crying and hysterical, shouting 'She's choking!'

followUp.question: What is your immediate action to relieve this severe choking?

options.text: Lean her forward and deliver up to 5 sharp back blows; if unsuccessful, give up to 5 abdominal thrusts
Perform a blind finger sweep to hook the biscuit out of her throat
Administer 2 rescue breaths and start chest compressions immediately
Encourage her to sit down and drink a glass of hot water

followUp.explanation: Conscious severe choking is treated with up to 5 back blows followed by up to 5 abdominal thrusts. Finger sweeps are dangerous as they can push the object further down. CPR is only for unresponsive patients. Choking patients must never be given fluids.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Position her leaning forward. Deliver firm slaps between the shoulder blades. If unsuccessful, perform abdominal thrusts. Call 999 if the airway remains blocked.
levelFlags.erNotes: Manage severe choking. If she loses consciousness, support her to the floor, call 999, and immediately begin CPR starting with chest compressions (visualizing the airway before ventilation).
